classification.difficultyReason: Determine corresponding vertices across differently oriented triangles and write them in matching order. The unscaffolded parts require recognising RHS or using equal-side marks to establish SSS with proportional sides.

content.prompt:
Write a similarity statement for these pairs of similar triangles; for example, $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$.
Be careful with the order of letters and make sure each letter matches the corresponding vertex.
Also state the reason.

spec.description: Paired upright triangles, smaller on the left; crosses match A with E and dots match C with D. Source blue outlines become ordinary black house-style geometry.
spec.mathematics: A corresponds to E, B to F, and C to D. Two marked pairs of corresponding angles are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Vertex labels and angle marks are permanent givens; the similarity statement and completed reason are answers.

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle EFD$ (AAA). At least two pairs of equal corresponding angles.
answer.worked: $\angle A=\angle E$ and $\angle C=\angle D$, so the third pair is also equal. Hence $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle EFD$ (AAA).

spec.description: Side-by-side triangles with opposite orientations. Preserve lengths 7 cm, 6 cm, 12 cm and 14 cm and equal-angle dots at B and D; ordinary geometry is black.
spec.mathematics: DF/AB = DE/BC = 2; the included angles B and D match. A corresponds to F and C to E.
spec.answerVisibility: All lengths, vertex names and dots are permanent givens.

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle FDE$ (SAS). Two pairs of corresponding sides in the same ratio and the included angle equal.
answer.worked:
$\begin{aligned}\frac{DF}{AB}&=\frac{14}{7}=2\\\frac{DE}{BC}&=\frac{12}{6}=2\end{aligned}$
The included angles $\angle ABC$ and $\angle FDE$ are equal. Hence $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle FDE$ (SAS).

spec.description: Small upper-left and larger lower-right right triangles, retaining the reflected orientation, right-angle squares at B and E and all supplied labels.
spec.mathematics: AC and DF are hypotenuses. DF/AC = 15/5 = 3 and EF/BC = 12/4 = 3. A corresponds to D, B to E, C to F.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements, vertex names and right-angle squares are visible in the question.

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ (RHS). The hypotenuses and another pair of corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
answer.worked:
$\angle ABC=\angle DEF=90^\circ$.
$\begin{aligned}\frac{DF}{AC}&=\frac{15}{5}=3\\\frac{EF}{BC}&=\frac{12}{4}=3\end{aligned}$
The hypotenuses and another pair of corresponding sides are in the same ratio. Hence $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ (RHS).

spec.description: Larger left-pointing equilateral triangle with double ticks on every side and smaller right-pointing equilateral triangle with single ticks on every side. Preserve 5 mm on CA and 2 mm on DE.
spec.mathematics: Each larger side is 5 mm and each smaller side is 2 mm. All three corresponding side ratios are 2/5; any consistent vertex bijection is valid.
spec.answerVisibility: Ticks, vertex labels and the two supplied lengths remain visible; inferred lengths and similarity statements are answers.

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ (SSS). Three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
answer.worked:
The equal-side marks give $AB=BC=CA=5\text{ mm}$ and $DE=EF=FD=2\text{ mm}$.
$\displaystyle\frac{DE}{AB}=\frac{EF}{BC}=\frac{FD}{CA}=\frac25$.
Hence $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF$ (SSS): three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
